x.name: alphaXiv
x.bio: High fidelity research

tweets.text:
"Perturbing Inputs Improves Pretraining Distillation"

Knowledge distillation normally trains a smaller LLM to copy a teacher's predictions on regular text, but this paper finds that deliberately corrupting the inputs can actually improve learning.

This paper trains students to match their teachers on perturbed inputs, such as blending neighboring tokens together, before switching back to normal distillation.

Across 135M and 0.5B models, this reduces validation loss by 0.025 and 0.020 nats, respectively, compared to standard distillation. At 0.5B, it also improves average zero-shot accuracy by 1% across 7 tasks.

https://t.co/76uN4g4kqO

Agent swarms are the next scaling frontier for AI.

For years, we’ve scaled intelligence by training larger models and giving them more time to think. But there’s another dimension: running many agents in parallel, exploring different approaches, challenging each other, and working together on solutions that no single agent could easily discover.

OpenAI has already demonstrated the potential of this approach with breakthroughs in mathematics.

Until now, experimenting with agent swarms yourself required building complicated orchestration infrastructure.

Starting today on Replit, spinning up a swarm of agents is just one prompt away.
